title: Adaptive canonical baseline for p95 and tokens/sec PR gating
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: implement a robust, low-false-positive CI gate that detects meaningful regressions in p95 latency and tokens/sec for PRs. The approach creates a canonical baseline per model/route by combining rolling historical summaries, stratified workload slices, and an auto-calibrated smoothing step. We will use spline-based trend anchoring and bootstrap confidence intervals over slices so the gate adapts to seasonality and avoids reacting to transient microbursts. Key ideas:

- Canonical baseline: compute a weighted rolling median and interquartile range over the last N successful CI runs per slice (slice = model+seq_len_bucket+batch_profile). Weight recent runs more heavily.
- Spline smoothing: apply a low-degree spline to the series of medians to remove short-term churn while preserving directional shifts.
- Confidence estimation: bootstrap per-slice token-level samples to estimate p95 CI and tokens/sec variance; aggregate across slices using an entropy-weighted scheme to prioritize high-traffic slices.
- KV warmup and priming: incorporate a warmup phase (KV-cache priming traces) into the baseline computation for sequences where cold-start noise is significant.
- Autocalibration: dynamic thresholds computed per-route using historical noise floor; default to conservative thresholds (e.g., block-if p95 > baseline + max(10%, 3*std)) but allow temporary relaxations when baseline uncertainty is large.
- PR gating semantics: a PR is blocked only if (a) there is a statistically significant regression with >= 95% confidence and (b) regression affects a weighted-traffic share above a configurable threshold (default 5%). A softer alert path surfaces lower-confidence degradations to the author and perf team.

This ticket covers the baseline computation service, CI integration hooks (reporting + decision APIs), and initial dashboards for triage. Implementation must be resilient to noisy CI runs and include a debug mode to replay traffic slices for post-mortem analysis.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha G: Created ticket after spike where several PRs produced p95 noise. Proposal drafted and reviewed with runtime team.

2025-02-12 - Liam C: Ran a small experiment on canary model `redwood-alpha` with 30 historical runs; spline smoothing removed several false positives. Added dataset artifacts to Drive (link in attachments).

2025-02-17 - Marco Salazar: Reviewed aggregation approach; recommended using traffic-entropy weighting rather than absolute tokens/sec to avoid overemphasizing long-tail slices.

acceptance_criteria: Service computes canonical baseline per model+slice and exposes baseline summary API
CI hook calls decision API and returns PASS/WARN/BLOCK according to the autocalibrated thresholds
Dashboards show baseline, recent runs, spline-smoothed trend and CI bands for each slice
False-positive rate measured on historical dataset is <= 2% for candidate thresholds
Debug replay mode can reproduce a gated run with raw token-level traces
decisions: Use rolling median + spline smoothing rather than exponential moving average to be robust to outliers
Bootstrap token-level resampling for CI on p95 rather than assuming normality
Weight slices by traffic-entropy to compute aggregated regression signal
follow_ups: ENG-473001 - Add CI worker autoscaler to run baseline warmup traces in parallel
ENG-473020 - Implement audit logging for gating decisions and store decision rationale
PM-401 - Document gating policy for customer-facing SLOs
environment: CI (GitHub Actions) + ephemeral perf runners (k8s) + baseline service (internal runtime namespace)
notes: We should run a 2-week shadow run where the gate produces decisions but does not block merges to gather real-world signal before enabling enforcement. Also include a canary config that applies only to low-traffic routes to validate behavior without customer impact.
